title: Mobility Foundations
notes: Hello Mary! Here is a workout plan with 3 days of exercises to work through. They are designed to be short strength training workouts that you can do each day as they will target different areas. I hope these will help you! If you experience pain, or you feel the exercise is not working, please send me a note with your Check-In at the end of the workout or an email if you notice something at a later day. Enjoy! Colleen~ Here is a link to videos for warmups; only do the movements that feel safe and work for you. https://youtu.be/at0krfIdgx4

warmup.name: Rowing Machine
warmup.cues: Use it as a warmup or for performance! A very versatile exercise!
warmup.coachingFocus: Be very aware of your form.
warmup.startWeight: Start with 500m and increase distance and speed slowly if it doesn't bother your hips.

warmup.name: Wall Angels
warmup.cues: Stand with back flat against wall. Slide arms up and down in Y-T-W pattern.

warmup.name: Chest/Deltoid Stretch
warmup.cues: Start with your good arm first. Test slowly how far you can reach without pain. Goal is to have both arms back and pull elbows toward spine.
warmup.progression: Do not force range — test your pain threshold to find your pain-free limit

primary.name: Pushups Against the Wall
primary.cues: Core engaged, don't let hips drop. Hands below shoulder height. Adjust to avoid wrist pain.
primary.progression: Move hands/ball lower to increase difficulty

primary.name: DB Chest Press
primary.cues: Control descent. Pause at chest. Drive up.

primary.name: DB Flys — Flat Bench
primary.cues: Wide arc with slight elbow bend. Feel chest stretch at bottom.

primary.name: DB Bicep Curl
primary.cues: Elbows stay at sides. Full range of motion — extend fully at bottom. Control the descent.
primary.progression: Add weight when 12 reps feel fully controlled
primary.startWeight: 8lbs 3 x 8 reps - don't take all the way to the shoulder.

primary.name: Bicep Hammer Curls
primary.cues: Keep your elbows tight to your body.
primary.startWeight: 8lbs 3 x 8 reps = keep elbows locked to side.

accessory.name: Pec Dec
accessory.cues: You can do this with or without weights for mobility. For strength make sure you can keep your elbows up with the weight.
accessory.contraindications: Do not work through any shoulder pain.
accessory.progression: Try without weights if you cannot keep form.

accessory.name: Robots
accessory.cues: Keep arms low to start. Palms facing outward. Keep elbows at comfortable level as you turn palms down. NO pain. Stay low and work slow.
accessory.progression: Goal image is the end point — not the starting point. Progress gradually

conditioning.name: Deadbug
conditioning.cues: Rest head on floor. Do not let lower back arch when straightening leg.

conditioning.name: Single-Leg Bridge
conditioning.cues: Start with both feet on floor. Lift hips as high as you can with no back pain. When stable, lift one leg and hold 10 seconds. Keep hips level.
conditioning.progression: If back pain or hamstring cramp occurs, lower hips. Progress to full bridge before single-leg
conditioning.startWeight: stay with both feet until you have had success with hips for a bit.

warmup.name: Leg Swings
warmup.cues: Light support if needed. Swing from hip, not low back. Control both directions.

warmup.name: Lateral Lunges
warmup.cues: Drive from heel of bent knee
warmup.startWeight: stationary - feet wide, reach your butt out back and feel adductors stretch.

warmup.name: High Knees
warmup.cues: Drive knee to hip height. Stay tall. Increase speed only if posture stays controlled.

warmup.name: Hip Openers
warmup.cues: Relax shoulders, ribs down, tall spine

primary.name: Band Leg Lifts
primary.startWeight: use a looser band, make sure you do not lean. :)

primary.name: Band Lateral Leg Lifts
primary.cues: Make sure you stand straight and not lean to the side. Lift as high as you can while balancing on the other leg.
primary.contraindications: Don't work through unreasonable hip pain.
primary.progression: Don't lift leg as high if it is too difficult.
primary.startWeight: use a loose band if you want to try a band, soft knee, posture ballerina - you want to feel abductors and obliques.

primary.name: Wall Sit with Pilates Ball
primary.cues: Make sure you press your bodyweight into the wall and your knees stay behind your toes. Squeeze the ball to activate your adductors. Try a 10 second hold at the end to feel the muscle work in an isometric hold.
primary.coachingFocus: Stability for adductors and isometric for quads and glutes
primary.contraindications: If you have knee pain, try not to bend as far down, or get a larger ball to avoid inner knee pain.
primary.progression: Add weight for progression, remove ball for regression
primary.startWeight: do a heel raise on one foot to work harder.

primary.name: Machine Leg Press - Single Leg
primary.cues: Make sure the weight is much lighter than you would use with both feet on the pad.
primary.contraindications: if you feel hip or knee pain, stop.
primary.progression: IF it is too difficult, try the leg extension machine with 1 leg.
primary.startWeight: Work your way to single lage - make sure weight is light.

primary.name: Machine - Single Leg Extension
primary.cues: Do not continue with Single-leg if it causes pain.

primary.name: Single-Leg Deadlift
primary.cues: Hinge from hip. Maintain long spine. Working leg soft.
primary.startWeight: Use walking stick, heel and butt against wall.

conditioning.name: Windshield Wipers
conditioning.cues:
T-Position: Lie on your back, arms out wide for support, legs straight up.
Side Sweep: Lower your legs to one side while keeping both shoulders down.
Core Pull: Use your obliques to pull the legs back to the center.
Controlled Arc: Move slowly; don't let gravity take over at the bottom.

conditioning.name: Forearm Plank
conditioning.cues:
Cues: 
Place elbows under shoulders and actively push the floor away to spread your shoulder blades.
Tuck your tailbone and pull your ribs toward your hips to slightly round your lower back.
Tighten your glutes and core as if someone is about to punch your stomach.
Keep your gaze on the floor for a long neck and maintain steady, deep breaths.

warmup.name: Arm Swings
warmup.cues: Relax shoulders, ribs down, tall spine

warmup.name: Wall Angels
warmup.cues: Stand with back flat against wall. Slide arms up and down in Y-T-W pattern.

primary.name: Pushups Against the Wall
primary.cues: Core engaged, don't let hips drop. Hands below shoulder height. Adjust to avoid wrist pain.
primary.progression: Move hands/ball lower to increase difficulty

primary.name: Lat Pulldowns
primary.cues: Pull bar to chin. Squeeze lats. Control return.
primary.progression: Increase load when form is solid
primary.startWeight: Use a band to protect your shoulder, pull band in front and toward your chin.

primary.name: DB Tricep Kickbacks
primary.cues: Elbows locked to side. Elbows above body height. Neutral spine — look 45° down.
primary.progression: Stay in deep lunge for additional challenge

primary.name: Front Raises
primary.cues: Stand tall, ribs down. Soft bend in elbows. Raise arms straight in front. Stop before shoulder height. Lower slowly.
primary.progression: Increase range only when pain-free. Stay below your pain threshold

accessory.name: Lateral Arm Raises
accessory.cues: Stand tall, ribs down. Soft bend in elbows. Lift arms out to the side toward shoulder height. Lower slowly with control.
accessory.progression: Add very light weight only when fully pain-free at shoulder height

conditioning.name: Hollow Body Hold
conditioning.cues:
Press lower back into the floor; tuck tailbone to round.
Reach arms overhead and hover legs just off the floor.
Shape like a Banana: Keep your shoulder blades and heels lifted; back stays glued.
Breathe shallow and keep everything braced like a rock.
conditioning.startWeight: try holding this position for 5-10 seconds and see how it goes. :)
